documents.unit: Student Code of Conduct (Worldwide student handbook page)
documents.title: Student Code of Conduct: Academic Integrity, Artificial Intelligence (AI)
documents.stance_why: The section says students 'may use AI to support learning and productivity when its use is consistent with course objectives, assignment requirements, and instructor or supervisor directions' and that students must follow 'instructor-specific restrictions'. It sets no uniform rule and defers to courses and instructors, with encouragement of AI fluency, so delegates.
documents.summary: The AI section of the student conduct code defines AI misuse as an academic integrity violation, encourages AI fluency, and lists appropriate learning uses. It makes students responsible for verifying output, following data security rules, and complying with course-level disclosure and instructor restrictions.

units.why: Defines AI misuse as a violation: 'Using artificial intelligence or automated technologies in violation of University, program, course or instructor requirements'. It classes unauthorized or misrepresented AI use as an academic integrity violation, so P36; it binds students and applies when misuse occurs.
units.anchor: Using artificial intelligence or automated technologies in violation of University, program, course or instructor requirements

units.why: Lists specific forms of misuse: 'misrepresentation of AI-generated work, fabrication or falsification of information, or use of AI to facilitate other prohibited conduct'. Chosen P36 (misconduct classification) because it names violations, not disclosure rules.
units.anchor: misrepresentation of AI-generated work, fabrication or falsification of information

units.why: Principle for AI in education: 'must be guided by ethical principles and academic integrity'. It is an institution-level framing statement, so P56.
units.anchor: must be guided by ethical principles and academic integrity

units.why: States 'encourages students to develop fluency in artificial intelligence', a career/development rationale for AI use, so P44; the university welcomes AI.
units.anchor: encourages students to develop fluency in artificial intelligence

units.why: 'students are expected to engage thoughtfully and responsibly with these technologies' is a general expectation of responsible use, a framework principle (P56) rather than a specific permitted or prohibited use.
units.anchor: students are expected to engage thoughtfully and responsibly with these technologies

units.why: 'Students may use AI to support learning and productivity when its use is consistent with course objectives' sets a conditional default permission, so P02. P04 (instructor decides) also fits but the sentence first grants permission, with instructor direction as a condition.
units.anchor: Students may use AI to support learning and productivity when its use is consistent

units.why: 'AI use should strengthen, and not replace, the student's own understanding, judgment, intellectual effort' says AI must not replace the student's thinking, so P32.
units.anchor: AI use should strengthen, and not replace, the student’s own understanding, judgment

units.why: Example of appropriate use: 'Clarifying difficult concepts or receiving explanations', i.e. AI as a tutor, so P12.
units.anchor: Clarifying difficult concepts or receiving explanations.

units.why: 'Practicing language, coding or problem-solving skills' is a listed appropriate use for practice and self-study, so P14 (not P13, as debugging is not mentioned).
units.anchor: Practicing language, coding or problem-solving skills.

units.why: 'Creating non-graded examples, scenarios or visuals to support learning' is a study-aid use limited to non-graded material, so P14.
units.anchor: Creating non-graded examples, scenarios or visuals to support learning.

units.why: 'Supporting course learning activities where permitted by the instructor' makes the use depend on the instructor's permission, so P04.
units.anchor: Supporting course learning activities where permitted by the instructor.

units.why: 'Students are responsible for evaluating and verifying any material produced, summarized, transformed or suggested by AI tools' requires checking AI output for errors, so P31.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for evaluating and verifying any material produced, summarized, transformed or suggested

units.why: 'Use of AI must comply with: Embry-Riddle's Academic Integrity Policy' ties AI use to the existing integrity policy; it is a scope/framework rule, P56.
units.anchor: Use of AI must comply with:

units.why: 'IT and data security policies. For more information, see Embry-Riddle AI Resources' requires AI use to comply with data security rules and points to university resources, so P50.
units.anchor: IT and data security policies. For more information, see Embry-Riddle AI Resources.

units.why: AI use must follow 'Course- or program-specific guidelines (e.g., syllabus statements or assignment instructions), including expectations for disclosure and labeling of AI-generated content.' Disclosure and labeling is the load-bearing rule, so P24; the delegation to syllabi is secondary.
units.anchor: including expectations for disclosure and labeling of AI-generated content.

units.why: 'Students are responsible for understanding and following any instructor-specific restrictions on AI use' delegates restrictions to instructors and makes students responsible for knowing them, so P04.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for understanding and following any instructor-specific restrictions on AI use.

units.why: Under Fraud: 'including the unauthorized use of AI technology' counts unauthorized AI use as deceit, so misconduct classification, P36.
units.anchor: including the unauthorized use of AI technology.

notes: Only the AI section (about lines 1181-1214) of the handbook was coded, plus the Fraud line that mentions AI. No computing-specific document exists.
